rules.title: RSO relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: For units under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, every no-fault eviction requires relocation assistance and filing a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before notice is served. No-fault grounds are listed in LAMC 151.09.A.8, A.10 to A.14: owner, relative or resident-manager occupancy; demolition or removal from rental use (Ellis Act, LAMC 151.22-151.28); government order to vacate; HUD sale; residential hotel conversion; affordable housing conversion. A copy of the termination notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 days of service. Payment is per unit and must be made available within 15 days of service of the notice, or placed in escrow. Mom and Pop owners (building of 4 or fewer units; owner has no more than 4 units plus one SFD in LA) may pay reduced amounts for owner or relative occupancy evictions (LAMC 151.30).
rules.key_value: For 7/1/2026-6/30/2027: Eligible tenants $11,000 (<3 yrs) or $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified tenants $23,150 or $27,400; Mom & Pop owner-occupancy: $10,550 / $21,250. Adjusted every July 1.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the LA RSO (certificate of occupancy on or before 1978-10-01).
rules.exemptions: No relocation is owed when replacing a resident manager with another resident manager, or when eviction is required by hazardous conditions from a natural disaster not caused by the landlord. Accumulated unpaid rent may be offset against relocation, except where the termination is required by a government order to vacate. Mom and Pop reduced amounts apply only to owner or relative occupancy evictions in buildings of 4 or fewer units.
rules.interaction: Where a Protected Unit is demolished for new construction and the tenant is lower income, the RPO and state HCA amounts apply if higher.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1 (§ 151.09)
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction an RSO violation. Tenant may raise non-payment of relocation as an affirmative defense in an eviction action, file an LAHD complaint, or pursue a private right of action.

rules.title: Just Cause Ordinance relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: For units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance, no-fault terminations require relocation assistance and filing a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before notice is served. No-fault grounds are listed in LAMC 165.03.H to M: owner, relative or manager occupancy; demolition or removal from rental use; government order to vacate; HUD sale; residential hotel conversion; affordable housing conversion. A copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 days. Payment is due within 15 days of service of the notice, or placed in escrow.
rules.key_value: For 7/1/2026-6/30/2027: Eligible $11,000 / $14,400; Qualified $23,150 / $27,400; Mom & Pop owner-occupancy reduced amounts. Single-family dwelling owned by a natural person (owning no more than 4 units plus one SFD in LA): one month's rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the LA Just Cause Ordinance (LAMC ch. XVI, art. 5).
rules.exemptions: Single-family dwellings owned by natural persons pay one month's rent (LAMC 165.06.A.6). Accumulated unpaid rent may be offset, except where the termination is required by a government order to vacate (LAMC 165.06.J). Reduced Mom & Pop amounts apply only to owner or relative occupancy evictions in buildings of 4 or fewer units.
rules.interaction: Where a Protected Unit is demolished for new construction and the tenant is lower income, the RPO and state HCA amounts apply if higher.
rules.quoted_span: laws require all tenants be paid relocation assistance in the amounts required by the RSO or JCO
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Declaration makes the eviction a JCO violation. Tenant has an affirmative defense, may file an LAHD complaint, and has a private right of action.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units
rules.requirement: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must comply with RPO relocation requirements. Lower-income households receive enhanced relocation through one of three options: standardized payment, comparable replacement unit plus RSO/JCO amounts, or an individualized relocation plan. The owner pays the highest applicable State or City amount. Tenants also have a right to remain up to 6 months before construction (including a 6-month move-out notice), a right to return if demolition does not proceed, and a right of first refusal for some tenants.
rules.key_value: Standardized payments for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027: Extremely Low Income $115,480; Very Low $96,750; Low $87,450. Above low income households receive RSO/JCO amounts.
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected Units demolished for new construction. Protected Units include all RSO units, units under an affordability covenant or rent control within the past 5 years, units rented by lower-income households within the past 5 years, and units withdrawn under the Ellis Act within the past 10 years.

coverage.other_unknown_fact: Whether the unit is a Protected Unit (e.g., recorded affordability covenant or prior rent control within 5 years, or Ellis withdrawal within 10 years) for non-RSO buildings

rules.exemptions: Above low-income households and non-Protected Units receive regular RSO/JCO relocation.
rules.interaction: Codifies and expands state Housing Crisis Act occupant protections. The owner pays the higher of State or City amounts.
rules.citation: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance)
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.conflict_note: The document gives February 11, 2025 as both the Council adoption date and the effective date; city ordinances usually take effect after publication, so verify the effective date.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower-income occupants displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of a protected unit for new construction must receive relocation benefits equal to those public entities must pay under Gov. Code § 7260 et seq.
rules.key_value: Relocation consistent with Gov. Code § 7260 et seq. for lower-income (≤80% AMI) displaced occupants
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected units demolished for new housing development projects.

coverage.other_unknown_fact: Whether the unit is a protected unit (affordability covenant, rent control, or Ellis withdrawal history)

rules.interaction: In Los Angeles, the owner pays the higher of HCA or City (RSO/JCO/RPO) amounts.
rules.quoted_span: 3. Pay relocation assistance to tenants in compliance with the State law’s Housing Crisis Act

rules.title: Relocation for demolition or condominium/commercial conversion (LAMC 47.06-47.07)
rules.requirement: Landlords who demolish a property or convert it to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels, or commercial uses must pay relocation assistance, whether or not the property is under the RSO or JCO. Once a tentative map for condominium conversion is approved, tenants may elect to relocate without a termination notice and still receive relocation.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance required for demolition or conversion regardless of RSO/JCO status
rules.coverage_conditions: Demolition or conversion of residential rental property in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: of whether the property is subject to the RSO OR JCO (LAMC 47.06 & 47.07).
